messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created — Elevated latency spike in streaming endpoints (us-west-2). Alerting on p95 > 1200ms, p99 > 4000ms. Root: potential KV cache pressure and fragmentation causing prefill vs decode imbalance. Pager: Maria (oncall)
Maria (oncall): I'm investigating. Seeing big jumps in tail latencies aligned with KV eviction spikes ~10:02 UTC. Streaming stalls reported by 3 customers so far.
Maria (oncall): Quick metrics snapshot from dashboard: p50 95ms, p95 1.3s, p99 4.5s for /v1/stream. KV hit-rate down 18% -> sudden prefill churn.
Devon K.: hitting the same graphs. KV slab utilization shows lots of small fragments; eviction rate spiked 6x at 10:01. Prefill queue length increased.
Liam SRE: logs show repeated prefill->decode contention on the same shards. Decode CPU saturating on a subset of workers.
Maria (oncall): hypothesis: fragmentation + aggressive prefill is causing many prefill requests that compete with decode, pushing streaming tails over SLO.
Tara PM: customers seeing partial streams / stalls after initial tokens? Any customer-visible error codes?
Maria (oncall): no 5xx spike, mostly long streams that pause for seconds and then resume. Looks like KV misses cause blocking prefill RPCs that delay next token generation.
Aj Patel: can we temporarily reduce prefill aggressiveness or throttle prefill priority for streaming routes?
Liam SRE: yes. Two mitigation knobs we can flip fast: 1) lower prefill concurrency and make prefill lower priority than decode; 2) increase per-shard slab size on affected hosts. I can flip (1) now.
Maria (oncall): do it. Command to flip prefill concurrency (admin CLI):
```
# reduce prefill concurrency to 2 for streaming route in us-west-2
redwoodctl runtime set --region us-west-2 --route /v1/stream cache.prefill.max_concurrency=2
```
Devon K.: also suggest disabling background prefill for longest-session routes for 15m. That will avoid extra KV pressure while we stabilize.
Liam SRE: executing change now. Patching config -> prefill priority lowered, concurrency set to 2. Rolling config -> workers in us-west-2 will pick up in ~30s.
incident-bot: Config change deployed to 12 workers. Monitoring for 5 minutes.
Maria (oncall): metrics after change (10:10 UTC): p95 dropped to 650ms, p99 2100ms. KV eviction rate down 40%. Early signal looks positive.
Tara PM: sending note to CS: "We are actively mitigating streaming stalls; partial stalls may have occurred for ~15-20 mins. We'll update in 30m."
Aj Patel: good. Can we also route heavy long-tail customers temporarily to a smaller model variant (lower memory footprint) to reduce KV working set?
Devon K.: yes we have a compatible variant. I can enable route override for top 2 impacted customers. Command:
```
# route override for customer A and B to model-x-small for 20m
redwoodctl route override --customer customerA --model model-x-small --duration 20m
redwoodctl route override --customer customerB --model model-x-small --duration 20m
```
Maria (oncall): please run those.
Devon K.: applied. Routing changes live.
Liam SRE: continuing to watch decode CPU per-host. Still seeing a couple of machines with high decode queue length; planning a rolling restart of those workers to trigger slab compaction. ETA 8m for restart window.
Maria (oncall): agree, do a rolling restart one node at a time to avoid added capacity loss. Add health-check gating.
Liam SRE: rolling restart started for host inf-uw2-17. Next host in 3m if stable.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident update — mitigation in progress. Initial mitigations lowered prefill concurrency, route overrides applied, rolling restarts started.
Maria (oncall): current status (10:20 UTC): p95 420ms, p99 1200ms, KV eviction rate normalized. Streaming stalls reports dropping. I'm going to run a quick end-to-end tail test against the streaming route to validate continuity.
Aj Patel: taking the secondary pager and will lead through remainder of incident. Maria — handing off at 10:22 UTC. Handoff summary: root cause suspected KV cache fragmentation causing prefill/decode imbalance; mitigations applied: lowered prefill concurrency, disabled background prefill for long sessions, route overrides for 2 customers, rolling restarts for compaction. Next steps: monitor for 30m, if p99 > 2s revert route overrides and consider temporary capacity burst or increase slab allocation.
Maria (oncall): confirmed handoff. Logs and notes in #runbooks/kv-eviction (link) and I'll leave a short runbook snippet below.
Maria (oncall): Runbook snippet:
```
1) If p99 > 2s and eviction rate > baseline*2 -> increase per-shard slab target on affected hosts: redwoodctl runtime set --host <host> cache.slab.target_mb=8192
2) If decode CPU > 85% on >20% hosts -> start rolling restart with health-check gating
3) Temporary route overrides -> use model-x-small for top offenders (20-30m)
4) If mitigations fail -> engage infra to provision short-lived extra capacity pool (Dedicated burst)
```
Aj Patel: I'll watch for 30m and coordinate with CS for customer comms if any regressions. Tagging oncall-rota for awareness.
oncall-rota: acknowledged.
incident-bot: Incident marked "mitigation in progress". Next automated check at 10:40 UTC.
Maria (oncall): leaving the channel, ping me if anything spikes. Good handoff Aj.
Aj Patel: thanks — will update at 10:40 or earlier."
